Merger Agreement: SECTION 9.3. Evaluation of Acquisition Proposals. <omitted> (e) During the Evaluation Period, the Company Board shall consider any Acquisition Proposal received from a third party and determine whether it constitutes a Superior Proposal. This determination shall be made in good faith, after consultation with the Company’s financial advisors and outside legal counsel, taking into account (i) the financial terms of the proposal, including any adjustments to the purchase price, (ii) the strategic fit of the proposal with the Company’s long-term business strategy, (iii) any legal implications that may arise from the proposal, and (iv) the potential impact on the Company’s employees and stakeholders. The Company shall provide the Parent with a written notice detailing the terms of the Superior Proposal and allow for a negotiation period of five Business Days, during which the Parent may propose amendments to the current Agreement. If the Company Board, after considering any such amendments, still determines that the Acquisition Proposal remains a Superior Proposal, it may proceed with recommending the proposal to its shareholders. (Pages 82-83)
